title: This Frog Freezes Solid Every Winter, Heart Stopped, Then Wakes Up
subject: wood frog

scenes.text: This frog freezes solid, its heart stops, and it comes back to life.
The wood frog, less than three inches long, lets up to 60 percent of its body turn to ice.
It stops breathing. Its heart stops beating. For all anyone can tell, it's dead.
How it survives: when ice forms, its liver floods the blood with glucose, up to ten times normal.
That sugar acts like antifreeze, protecting the cells while the ice forms between them.
Some stay frozen for months, then thaw in spring, and hop away.

description:
The wood frog lets much of its body freeze solid each winter, with no heartbeat and no breathing, and thaws back to life.
Glucose from its liver protects its cells while ice forms around them.
Would you believe it if you found one frozen?
first_comment: Wood frogs go through 10 to 15 freeze-thaw episodes before they freeze for the season. Would you survive one?
